author: OverSite AI
body:
Resiliency, power quality, uptime and economics that show up on the P&L

Oil and gas operators are electrifying the field: electric frac spreads, larger camp blocks, more automation on production, and more intermittent or imported power at the fence line. That shift raises the bar for bus stability, power quality, and uptime outcomes often associated with advanced storage programs. OverSiteAI Power pursues those same outcomes from the prime-mover and microgrid side: dependable, gas-fueled generation and protection architecture sized for real pad loads, so your equipment sees clean voltage and frequency through step changes not just on day one, but across the whole campaign.

Natural gas prime power for the electrified pad

We package conditioned field gas or pipeline gas into generation that can shoulder electric frac support, large rotating loads, artificial lift, compression, and long-duration production displacing diesel where molecules are available and reducing truck traffic, rack exposure, and stack impact. Protection, grounding, and switchgear choices are built for simul-fracs, zipper moves, and winter ops, not lab demos. The goal is simple: keep the bus where your VFDs, pumps, and controls expect it, so production minutes and completion hours are not lost to power drama.

Power quality that protects equipment life

  • Voltage and frequency discipline — Ride through the harmonic-rich, stair-step load profiles that come with modern spreads.
  • Coordination with your electrification roadmap — Designs stay coherent when you add storage, utility import/export, or renewables tie-in; we do not treat the generator string as a permanent island in a vacuum.
  • Visibility — Telemetry lands where your engineers already work so trends, anomalies, and events are visible before they become callouts.

Safer operations, fewer “go fix the bus” moments

  • Logistics risk — Less distillate on the road, fewer midnight fuel windows fighting sand and water gates.
  • Controlled recovery — Sequencing and labeling that make restarts predictable after faults or weather so fewer adhoc trips during storms or off shift hours.
  • One narrative for Ops and Finance — The same metered story for AFE, emissions, and partner reporting.

Cash flow, not just kilowatts

We help you model fuel mix, heat rate, and contingency diesel with transparent assumptions, so savings from gas substitution, efficiency, and avoided downtime are defensible in the room where approvals happen. Where programs participate in demand response, peak management, or behind the meter strategies, we align generation dispatch and metering so you are not leaving revenue or credits on the table because the data never made it out of the field.

How we start

A practical 72-hour power study: gas availability, forecasted load steps, harmonic budget, storage or utility interfaces (if any), and tie-in sequencing. Then a joint mobilization plan, commissioning checklist, and hand back criteria so turnover is boring, in the best way.

title: OverSiteAI Field Lighting
body:
Light that matches the pace of modern pads

OverSiteAI Field Lighting delivers tower packages on the order of 100 feet of mast height and roughly 2.5 million lumens—enough to wash multi-well completions, SIMOPS corridors, and sand logistics lanes with even, specifiable lux—without turning night shift into a glare hazard.

Why super-pads need super-lumens

  • Walkdown velocity — Crews see connections, slips, and trip hazards the first pass—not the third.
  • CCTV and gate assurance — Cameras capture usable plates and faces instead of muddy silhouettes.
  • Neighbor management — Aimable arrays and zoning keep candela on lease road and rig floor, not the fence line.
  • Weather realism — Guy patterns, ice assumptions, and wind ratings baked into every plan—not bolted on after the first front.

Integrated with power strategy

Lighting load gets coordinated with OverSiteAI Power so fuel priority, harmonic budget, and breaker labeling stay coherent. Rapid skidding between zipper stages is choreographed with crane windows and SIMOPS maps—minimizing downtime between frac fleets.

What you receive

Photometric layout against your pad map, rig-up / rig-down checklist, and nightly lux verification protocol. If leadership wants before/after documentation for HSSE or community outreach, we package it camera-ready.

title: OverSiteAI Optics
body:
The digital thread for flowback, pumpdown, and everything between

OverSiteAI Optics is the operations layer that replaces scattered PDFs, radio stories, and three versions of the same spreadsheet. Tickets, BOLs, gauge sheets, and shift summaries generate automatically from field events—GPS on loads and assets stitches who, what, and where into a single auditable record.

Built for the no-sleep week

  • Flowback and pumpdown lenses — Stage timers, rate trends, and SIMOPS overlaps on one canvas—engineers stop reconciling CSV exports at breakfast.
  • Load traceability — Every gate exit, route, and offload tied to pad coordinates—no more “which truck was that?”
  • Exception routing — Geofence departures, rate deviations, or missed handoffs escalate to the channel that actually responds at 3 a.m.
  • Partner-ready exports — Midstream, JV, and regulatory packages drop with consistent naming, signatures, and attachments.

Operator-first capture

Minimal taps, offline-tolerant forms, and APIs that hydrate your data lake mean crews spend seconds—not minutes—logging reality. Optics is how you answer prove it when legal, partners, or the board asks what happened on pad last Tuesday.

Pilot playbook

Pick one pad workflow—pumpdown plus fluid haul, for example. We mirror it digitally in a 7-day pilot, measure adoption and error rate, then scale with training kits your captains actually use.

author: OverSite Services
subtitle: Clean swaps. Faster turns.
teaser: Reliable roll-off services for drilling, completions, and production locations. Proper placement, fast swaps, and execution that keeps your site safe and compliant.
title: Roll Off Boxes
body:
Reliable containers, on the schedule your job runs on

Roll-off services are simple in theory and brutal in execution. Containers get dropped late, stacked in the wrong spot, or sit full while your crew waits. We built our roll-off operation around the obvious goal: be where you need us, when you need us, with the right configuration in the right place—so site flow stays clean and waste streams stay compliant.

What we deliver

  • On-schedule placement and pickup tied to your operations cadence—drilling, completions, or production.
  • Clean swap-outs that reduce site congestion and minimize downtime when full containers cycle out.
  • Drop-off through pickup tracked digitally, with timestamped records that align with your closeout package.
  • Configurations sized to your waste streams—standard, sealed, or specialty—matched to volume, frequency, and disposal pathway.

Where it fits

Drilling pads, completion locations, production facilities, and yards. Anywhere a clean, well-staged roll-off operation reduces friction in the field.

Why it matters

Site safety and regulatory exposure live in the details: container placement relative to lay-down areas, segregation of waste streams, and documentation regulators actually review. Our crews and dispatch process treat roll-off as part of the operation, not an afterthought.

author: OverSite Services
subtitle: Protect what's downstream.
teaser: Turnkey filtration pod deployment for frac, flowback, and produced water. Built to reduce solids-related failures and hold consistent flow when it matters.
title: Filter Pods
body:
Filtration that protects your real investment

The cost of a solids-related failure downstream isn't the filter media—it's the pump, the seal, the line, and the hours your spread isn't producing. Our filter pod operation is built around protecting what's downstream: sized correctly for the job, deployed turnkey, swapped on schedule, and documented in line with field activity.

What we deliver

  • Filtration pods sized to job-specific flow rates—matched to solids loading, fluid characteristics, and target effluent quality.
  • Media changes coordinated with your crew schedule, so swaps don't interrupt critical operations.
  • Performance tracked with structured documentation—differential pressure, throughput, and media-life records that follow the equipment.
  • Engineered to protect downstream pumps and infrastructure—filtration is a wear-prevention strategy, not just a regulatory line item.

Where it fits

Frac operations, flowback events, and produced water management. Anywhere fluid quality determines the life of your downstream equipment.

Operational philosophy

Pods come with a plan: target flow, expected solids load, swap interval, and a fallback if conditions change. When the pad runs hotter than expected, our crews adjust dispatch instead of letting a media change become a failure cascade.

author: OverSite Services
body:
When something goes wrong, time is the variable that matters

Spills, overflows, and unplanned events don't keep business hours. The longer the response window, the bigger the environmental footprint, the deeper the regulatory exposure, and the more non-productive time burned. Our gap vac operation is built for rapid mobilization with disciplined execution—a fast on-site response that keeps both the field and the closeout under control.

What we deliver

  • Rapid dispatch for time-critical events—you call, we mobilize, with clear ETAs and an on-site lead identified before arrival.
  • Containment, recovery, and disposal coordinated end-to-end—you get one point of accountability instead of a phone tree.
  • Field documentation built to support HSE reporting—what was contained, when, by whom, and where it went.
  • Crew handoff aligned with your safety lead—our team integrates with your incident command, not around it.

Where it fits

Tank overflows, line breaks, frac spread response, completions cleanup, production location events. Any situation where minutes matter and the paper trail matters too.

What you get back

Containment outcome, environmental exposure minimized, NPT capped, and a documentation packet that holds up to internal review and regulatory inquiry.

title: Spill Remediation
body:
End-to-end response, with closeout regulators accept

Spill remediation isn't done when the surface looks clean—it's done when the file is closed. We run remediation as a complete project: assessment through containment, cleanup, regulatory thresholds, disposal manifests, and final documentation that holds up under audit.

What we deliver

  • Initial site assessment and containment—size up the release, stop the spread, secure the perimeter.
  • Soil and water remediation aligned with regulatory thresholds—work to defensible criteria, not just "looks better."
  • Disposal manifests and chain-of-custody tracking—every load accounted for, every signature in the right place.
  • Final closeout package built for audit readiness—the file regulators actually want to see.

Where it fits

Pad incidents, pipeline events, terminal and storage releases, transportation events. Wherever a hydrocarbon or produced-fluid release needs to move from incident to closed file.

Why operators bring us in

Speed matters in the first hours. Documentation matters in the last hours. We're built for both: fast on the response, disciplined through cleanup, and structured at closeout. Your environmental and legal teams get a packet they can defend.

author: OverSite Services
subtitle: Visibility without permanent infrastructure.
teaser: Short- or long-term smart camera deployment for frac sites, yards, SWDs, and remote locations. Verification, incident review, and oversight on demand.
title: Smart Camera Rentals
body:
Visibility on demand, without the infrastructure cost

Most operators don't need permanent cameras at every location—they need visibility for the duration of the job. Our smart camera rental program puts connected camera systems on your sites for as long as you need them, then takes them off when the project ends. No permanent install, no infrastructure project, no orphaned hardware after the campaign.

What we deliver

  • Connected camera systems with live monitoring and recorded review—mobile-accessible, cloud-backed, no NVR closet required.
  • Flexible deployment durations—project-based, monthly, or open-ended. Scale up at job kickoff and demobilize at closeout.
  • AI-assisted detection for high-priority events—motion, intrusion, and anomaly alerts surfaced through the platform instead of buried in 30 hours of footage.
  • No permanent infrastructure investment required—rental model means no capex, no install crews, no commissioning project.

Where it fits

Frac sites, equipment yards, SWDs, lay-down areas, and remote production. Anywhere temporary visibility, security, or incident review is worth more than a permanent install.

Use cases

Theft and trespass deterrence on yards. Verification of loads in and out of pad gates. Incident review when something happens that needs to be reconstructed. Documentation footage for regulatory or partner reporting.

author: OverSite Services
subtitle: Protect the wells you're already producing.
teaser: Proactive monitoring during frac ops to identify, document, and respond to pressure communication risks — before they cost you a producer.
title: Defensive Frac & Offset Well Loading
body:
Protecting producing wells during nearby frac activity

The economics of a frac hit are unforgiving. A communicating offset well can lose months of production, force a workover, or in the worst case, change the long-term performance of an asset that was already cash-flowing. Our defensive frac program exists for one reason: protect the wells you're already producing while frac operations move through the area.

What we deliver

  • Pre-frac offset well assessment and load planning—identify risk wells, document baseline conditions, plan loading strategy with the operator.
  • Real-time pressure monitoring during operations—surface pressure, casing pressure, and flow indicators tracked through the frac campaign.
  • Anomaly detection with rapid escalation—pressure communication signatures surface as alerts, not as reading-list items at the end of the shift.
  • Documentation packet supporting regulatory and post-frac analysis—the record your reservoir engineering and legal teams need.

Where it fits

Multi-well pad fracs, infill drilling near producing wells, and any operation where a producing asset sits inside the influence zone of upcoming frac activity.

Why it matters

Frac hits used to be discovered after the fact. Defensive frac programs catch the signature in real time, document what happened, and give engineering and legal a defensible record—whether the goal is to mitigate, recompense, or simply prove what occurred.
